newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares decline on profit-taking, FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares decline on profit-taking, FOMC.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on Tuesday in a market dominated by selling and hit by profit-taking but also affected by the FOMC meeting with dealers seeing correction but no dramatic falls ahead if the U.S. hikes rates.

"We've slipped ahead of FOMC, but profit-taking was the main reason. We could see moderate falls tomorrow if the U.S. raises rates but that is only natural, Danish shares have climbed solidly recently," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index lost 0.68 point to 121.37, while the KFX December future was untraded at 123.15.
All KFX shares suffered losses with FLS Industries and A.P. Moeller's 1912 A the only papers to buck the downward trend.
FLS nudged one crown up to close at 720, while D/S 1912 A put on 1,000 crowns to finish at 140,000.
Tele Danmark was again the day's busiest paper with 280,000 shares changing hands to end one crown lower at 277.
Novo Nordisk shed three crowns to 906.
Overall turnover for the day was a modest 661 million crowns.
